name: Caio del Rossi
bio:
Caio del Rossi is a Brazilian actor trained in Film and Television at CAV – Centro de Audiovisual, in São Bernardo do Campo, São Paulo, where he began his artistic journey. After completing the program, he deepened his training in the performing arts by enrolling in an Acting School in the city of São Paulo, developing techniques for both stage and on-camera performance. He is a member of the theater collective Último Ato.

In audiovisual work, his most recent project includes his participation in the dramatized documentary “Eloá the Hostage: Live on TV” (Netflix / Paris Filmes, 2025), directed by Cris Ghattas, in which he portrayed Everton Douglas, brother of Eloá Pimentel, in the reenactment scenes of the case. In film, he played Leonardo in the short “O Assassino do Boom / The Boom Killer” (Dir. Vitor Dividino and Mateus Guidoni, 2026).

In theater, Caio has taken part in various productions within the long-standing Projeto 7 Leituras, directed and produced by Eugênia Thereza de Andrade and based at SESC Bom Retiro for the past 20 years. Among his works are: “O Arco Desolado” (2025), directed by Mika Linz, in which he played the Spy; “Auto da Compadecida” (2025), directed by Kiko Marques, playing the Sacristan; “The Tempest” (2024), as Trinculo; and “A Midsummer Night’s Dream” (2024), in which he portrayed Thisbe, both also directed by Kiko Marques.

credits.title: The Boom Killer
credits.overview: A great tragedy occurs during the filming of a movie. In an unexpected twist, the renowned Detective Bones takes on the case, as he can sniff out that something isn’t right.

credits.title: Eloá the Hostage: Live on TV
credits.overview: A tragic hostage case from 2008 Brazil unfolds through unseen diary entries, family interviews, and media coverage, as a 15-year-old girl is held captive by her ex-boyfriend for 100 hours while TV networks broadcast it live.
